sections.title: The last piece of the at/to/from set
sections.content: -hoz/-hez/-höz means "to" or "toward" a person or place — it's the destination partner of -nál/-nél ("at") and -tól/-től ("from"), which you already know. Add it to a noun to say where you're headed, the same way -nál/-nél says where you are and -tól/-től says where you're coming from.

items.english: Károly is going to the church.

sections.content: Vowel harmony picks the shape exactly the way it always has: templom has back vowels, so it takes -hoz; pékség has front unrounded vowels, so it takes -hez; szülő has a front rounded vowel, so it takes -höz. Nothing new about the pattern, just a new suffix to slot into it.
